knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Line Perpendicular to a Line Through Two Points

question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-3,-5)$ and $(-10,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-2-(-5)}{-10-(-3)} \\  & =\frac{3}{-7} \\  & =- \frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (- \frac{3}{7})=-1\,⇒\,m=\frac{7}{3}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(-8,8).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-8 & =\frac{7}{3}(x-(-8)) \\ y-8 & =\frac{7}{3}(x+8) \\ y-8 & =\frac{7 x}{3} + \frac{56}{3} \\ y & =\frac{7 x}{3} + \frac{80}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Line Perpendicular to a Line Through Two Points

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(5,1)$ and is perpendicular to the line passing through the points $(-6,0)$ and $(-9,6).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-6,0)$ and $(-9,6):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{6-0}{-9-(-6)} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (-2)=-1\,⇒\,m=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(5,1).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-5) \\ y-1 & =\frac{x}{2} - \frac{5}{2} \\ y & =\frac{x}{2} - \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
